narratives.Description: bug(release): v0.119.11 Windows Step 5 hang at 1314/1334 under 60m — recover sub-15m suite wall-clock
narratives.Overview:
1. **Sequencer input refresh (blocks-finding discharge).** Refresh `packages/core/fixtures/vitest-file-durations.json` from the retained v0.119.11 / hang-kill tee via existing `duration-rank` scraper. Delete sub-30s seeded noise. Ensure measured entries for `durable-effect-acquisition/evaluate.test.ts`, `presentation-coverage/gates.test.ts`, and corrected `landed-filename.test.ts`. Validate every fixture key resolves to a real tip test file. Acceptance criterion 4 is this fixture land, not CHANGELOG paste alone (CHANGELOG/RELEASING still document top offenders + fix class).

2. **Host diagnosis (record, do not invent).** On the release host, record repeated Git/Node binary latency, executable paths/versions, and host load against the existing RELEASING stale-binary differential before attributing the regression solely to suite composition. Host repair requires explicit evidence; no silent AV exclusion / binary replace as this critique's product change.

3. **Cheapen class for the three unit-project git tail files.** Prefer `#4567` share-plus-reset (one init, state reset between cases) for `durable-effect-acquisition/evaluate.test.ts` first (largest per-case git-spawn count), leaving it in the **unit** project. Do **not** move these three into `spawn-heavy` (one win32 worker would serial-drain them). Apply the existing `#4591` / `#5022` cost-class playbook only where share-plus-reset / in-process is product-safe; refresh durations for measured newcomers.

4. **Search space includes pool/isolate.** Root-cause inventory for this arc must name `pool` / `poolOptions.forks.isolate` alongside spawn/git cost, worker count, suite composition, AV/spawn latency, and heavy files. First-ship does **not** flip `isolate: false`; that lever is a separately measured later cut after item 5's before/after number exists, sequenced after fixture refresh (injection/swarm lens: win32 `dangerouslyIgnoreUnhandledErrors` swallows bleed).

5. **Acceptance = measured green Step 5 path under unchanged 60m.** Keep `RELEASE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_*` at 60 and keep `#5026` Step 5 host no-coverage lane. First-ship success is a Windows production-shaped Step 5 / `ts:check-lane` that completes the selected suite with zero test failures, valid tip-SHA coverage-of-record, no `--skip-ci`, under the existing detector. Record SHA, suite size, conditions, elapsed time, and retained tee on this issue; also record same-tip ubuntu coverage-of-record duration as the ratio anchor. Clear the named durable-effect assertion failure from its actual error. Historical sub-15m remains the recovery aspiration; if first ship only proves reliable sub-60m, state that gap as a tracked performance residual.

6. **Settle sequencer partition before sizing the tail.** With one instrumented win32 run (or equivalent evidence), settle whether `DurationSequencer`'s project-name tiebreak re-serializes spawn-heavy ahead of unit contrary to the config's `groupOrder` refusal. Size cheapen against that settled shape.

7. **Non-goals / later.** No `RELEASE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_*` raise. No `maxWorkers` cut. No `sequence.groupOrder`. No moving the three tail files into `spawn-heavy`. No first-ship `poolOptions.forks.isolate: false`. `#635`-class residue and unrelated session ceremony stay out.

audit-targets: none

Round 1 open critique; dispatch SHA `1890550a2afa7a6aa46e2cd3e27813a1dee36a9a`, input ceiling 5894333864. `git rev-parse HEAD` matched. Reads used that SHA; no fetch, checkout, ingest, or product edits. I did not read sibling posts.

## Diagnose the host before binding a suite-only remedy
sharpens-framing
Evidence: Five serial `git --version` probes in this Windows critic session took 673, 650, 973, 568, and 746 ms (median 673 ms; first-probe-excluded median 698 ms). At the dispatch SHA, `docs/RELEASING.md` already prescribes repeated binary-latency probes above roughly 150 ms for Git and describes a stale-binary differential with a previously measured 40m-to-3.6m recovery. `vitest.config.ts` separately records historical Windows spawn-throughput contention. These are competing explanations, not proof that either explains this incident. This probe is current host evidence, not a recreation of the release workload.
Failure mode: Binding exclusively to test rewrites or worker-count tuning can spend substantial scope compensating for a host executable regression. Conversely, declaring AV or stale binaries causal from this small probe would overclaim.
Disposition: Keep root-cause work in the first ship. Record repeated Git/Node latency, executable paths/versions, host load, and the existing documented differential on the release host before attributing the regression. Any host repair must be explicitly evidenced; do not require an AV exclusion or silently replace binaries as part of this critique. Preserve a comparable before/after full-lane measurement.

## Reuse the existing scheduler and reduce actual spawn work
sharpens-framing
Evidence: A Node inventory using `git show <dispatch-sha>:<path>` checked the config and committed duration JSON. There are 110 duration entries. `durable-effect-acquisition/evaluate.test.ts` and `presentation-coverage/gates.test.ts` are absent from both the spawn-heavy list and the duration map; `vbrief-validate/landed-filename.test.ts` is in unit and already has a 155168 ms duration entry. Source inspection shows real Git fixture creation in all three; durable-effect mixes injected in-process cases with Git integration cases. Existing mechanisms include overlapping unit/spawn-heavy projects, a Windows unit cap of `max(1,min(12,floor(cpus*0.25)))`, one spawn-heavy worker, and `DurationSequencer` using committed durations with BaseSequencer fallback. The reporter already flushes completed files lasting at least 30s, and `duration-rank.ts` ranks those retained tee lines.
Failure mode: A new reporter or generic slowest-first proposal duplicates landed work. Moving every slow file into the one-worker project can create a longer serial drain; refreshing durations changes scheduling but does not remove Git process cost. The last completed file and a completion-only top-N also do not identify the twenty unfinished files or prove an idle tail.
Disposition: Use the retained incident tee and existing ranker first, explicitly distinguishing completed-duration evidence from unfinished work. Refresh the existing duration seed for measured newcomers. Prefer a bounded cheapen of the measured dominant fixture/spawn class, with before/after spawn counts and full-lane wall time. Split pure cases from real-Git cases where useful; preserve integration coverage for committed/staged/live bytes and failure behavior. Shared fixture reset must restore refs/index/worktree and authority artifacts between cases. Pool changes remain an evidence-backed fallback, not the default Bound remedy.

## Define recovery as a passing Step 5, not merely beating the timer
sharpens-framing
Evidence: `release/constants.ts` fixes 60 minutes. `runReleaseCheck` computes one deadline before dispatching native `task check`, rejects exit 124, verifies that `ts:check-lane` actually ran when completion evidence is available, and resolves green tip-SHA GHA coverage on success. `docs/RELEASING.md` and `release/preflight.ts` confirm that Windows release Step 5 already drops host coverage under #5026; ambient `task check` is a different instrument. The in-ceiling issue evidence reports one failed durable-effect test before termination. Closed #5107 documents a full ~44m suite that nevertheless failed on a test timeout. I did not reproduce the incident failure or run a full release in this process-only critique.
Failure mode: A faster isolated test run, cached suite stamp, or 59-minute run with an assertion failure could be presented as recovery while the production release remains blocked. Treating the historical sub-15m aspiration as already demonstrated would likewise overstate the evidence.
Disposition: Bind first-ship success to an actual Windows production Step 5 with the full selected suite executed, zero test failures, valid tip-SHA coverage-of-record, no skip-ci, and total Step 5 time below the unchanged 60m deadline. Record SHA, suite size, conditions, elapsed time, and retained tee. Resolve the named failed test from its actual error, not by assuming it is only a timeout. Retain sub-15m as the measured recovery target; if the first ship only establishes reliable sub-60m operation, state that gap and leave a tracked performance residual instead of claiming the baseline restored.

The strongest first-ship Bound shape I would accept is one measured recovery slice: establish the release-host baseline using existing diagnostics and tee ranking; remove the dominant confirmed cost (host fault if demonstrated, otherwise a bounded fixture/spawn refactor); refresh existing duration data where needed; and prove the complete passing production Step 5 under the unchanged detector. Keep the existing coverage authority and test assertions intact. I would not bind a speculative worker/pool redesign or another timeout raise. The strongest case for scheduling-only work is an observed long idle tail with otherwise healthy spawn latency; such evidence would change that choice. No blocking finding is asserted against this open root-cause scope.

## Strongest first-ship Bound I would accept

Keep `RELEASE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS` / `RELEASE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MINUTES` at **60** and keep the #5026 Step 5 host no-coverage lane (`isStep5HostNoCoverage` → `pnpm exec vitest run`). First-ship recovers Windows production Step 5 so it **completes under that existing detector without `--skip-ci`**.

Compose mechanisms already on tip at the dispatch SHA:

1. Rank offenders from a hang-kill-durable `.deft/check-tees/**` tee with `packages/core/src/ts-check-lane/duration-rank.ts` (#5027 / RELEASING.md). Last-completed-file is only a hang cursor.
2. Refresh `packages/core/fixtures/vitest-file-durations.json` from that no-coverage tee so `DurationSequencer` (#5028) arms cold release worktrees with current durations (fixture is still the interim seed).
3. Apply the existing #4591 / #5022 cost-class playbook to tee-ranked multi-minute git-spawn files that still live in the **unit** project: move into `spawnHeavyGlobs` and/or share-plus-reset / in-process where the product allows. Do not invent a new pool, a new hang ceiling, or a maxWorkers cut (#3480 / vitest.config comments already forbid that class of "fix").
4. Treat assertion failures on the same Step 5 path as a separate red class that must clear in the same green-under-60m batch (body tee signal: `durable-effect-acquisition/evaluate.test.ts` 1 failed).
5. Document top offenders and the fix class in CHANGELOG / RELEASING when landed.

Road-not-taken: another numeric raise of `RELEASE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_*` (named-cause and RELEASING already say cheapen-first; #5091 already at 60m). ## Summary

Windows production `task release` Step 5 (`ts:check-lane`) hit the 60-minute hang detector (exit 124) on the v0.119.11 cut tip. Suite reached **1314 / 1334** files before kill — twenty files short of completion. Tests used to finish in under ~15 minutes on this host class; Step 5 wall-clock has regressed through successive hang-detector raises (20→30→45→60) without recovering that baseline.

## Evidence (v0.119.11 cut, 2026-09-29)

- Tip: `bc060886b` on `master` (post policy allow + reconcile stamp).
- Pipeline: Steps 1–4 OK; Step 5 `task check` / `ts:check-lane` **FAIL exit 124**.
- Last completed test file: `packages/core/src/presentation-coverage/gates.test.ts` (1314/1334).
- Near-end slow/fail signal in tee: `packages/core/src/durable-effect-acquisition/evaluate.test.ts` (49 tests | 1 failed, ~277s) immediately before the last-file stamp.
- Early suite was spawn-heavy (multi-minute `landed-filename.test.ts` ~268s); pace later improved but still projected past 60m.
- Hang detector: `RELEASE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS` / `RELEASE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MINUTES` = **60** (raised under #5091). This issue is **cheapen / root-cause**, not another numeric raise.
- Prior related: #5022 / #5023 (20→30 + cheapen), #5024 (30→45), #5026 coverage-of-record, #5027/#5028 duration ranking, #5107 (v0.119.10 nearly-green ~44m + suite-load flake; operator skip-ci).

## Acceptance

1. Identify root cause of Windows Step 5 wall-clock regression vs historical <~15m (spawn/git cost, worker count, suite composition, AV/spawn latency, new heavy files).
2. Land cheapen remediations so a production `task release` Step 5 completes **under the existing 60m hang detector without `--skip-ci`**.
3. Prefer measured cost reduction over raising `RELEASE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_*` again.
4. Document top offenders (tee timeline / duration rank) and the fix class in CHANGELOG / RELEASING when landed.

## Operator note

v0.119.11 production cut may use `--skip-ci --allow-skip-ci=<this-issue>` under explicit incident review so the hang class does not block the tag; the next patch after the cheapen lands should cut without `--skip-ci`.
